root_cause.text: In the `hash:*` IPv4 range iteration for sets like hash:ip,mark, the loop unconditionally increments the IP iterator after processing each address, including after the last one, which can save a traversal state (`h->next.ip`) beyond the requested range and cause a subsequent retry to start from an unintended position.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the loop from `for (; ip <= ip_to; ip++)` to `for (; ip <= ip_to;)` and adds an explicit `if (ip == ip_to) break; ip++;` inside the loop body, preventing the iterator from advancing past `ip_to`. The CVE description and commit message both state that advancing the iterator once more can move the traversal state past the end of the request, leading to incorrect continuation on retry.
